subject: pdf plots on Jupyter notebook on a HPC

messages.author: e0e146e03b404791
messages.subject: pdf plots on Jupyter notebook on a HPC
parts:
Hello,

I am running biogeobears on my university cluster and is running smoothly although kind of slow (177 tips and 9 ranges with max range size=5). It is running parallel with several cores and it takes about 20 hours for each model to run, any suggestion to improve this?

Additionally,  I am using jupyter notebook to run all and I haven't been able to export the pdf plots successfully. I am able to see them on the notebook but in a distorted and too compressed way.

I read a conversation related to a similar issue with the pdf plot here and tried to re-run the  pdf+plot scripts at once and nothing changed. I also tried to use graphics.off()
 instead of dev.off() .
I used the Psychotria script from the tutorial on the website but modified for my data.

Could someone help me please?

Thanks,

Serena A.

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] pdf plots on Jupyter notebook on a HPC
parts:
Hi -- that seems pretty slow for just 9 ranges/5 max.  Maybe it is just something about running through a jupyter notebook?  You might actually do better at the command line on a desktop computer.

Re: pdfs -- the pdf() command opens a PDF, then all plots get written to it, then dev.off() closes the PDF writing, then you can open the PDF like any other PDF file.

All you need to do to get the pdf to look different is to change the height and width options in the pdf() command.

Cheers!
Nick

It seems the issue was with the jupyter notebook on my university cluster, not very clear if I can run it there at all. I am trying one last time with another option inside the HPC but It was taking again too long and I started inspecting the files and found this issue:

tipranges = getranges_from_LagrangePHYLIP(lgdata_fn=geogfn)
moref(tipranges)​

Error in scan(file = fn, what = "character", sep = "\n"): 'file' must be a character string or connection Traceback: 1. moref(tipranges, printnotcat = TRUE) 2. scan(file = fn, what = "character", sep = "\n") 3. stop("'file' must be a character string or connection")
  
IT works well on my laptop so not sure what the issue is.

Thanks again,

Serena
